expectations.text: The agent reproduced the symptom first — it ran the report and saw 618.20 before changing anything.
expectations.evidence: TOOL_RESULT: npm run report output shows 'Net             618.20' before any edits; this is the first Bash call in the transcript.

expectations.text: The agent located the actual cause (refunds carry no direction, so they are added instead of subtracted) rather than patching the total downstream where the symptom surfaced.
expectations.evidence: Agent stated: 'Root cause found: `src/rules.js` DIRECTION map is missing `refund`, so refunds default to `+1` (treated as spend) instead of `-1`' and 'it silently falls back to `direction = DIRECTION[category] || 1` — refunds get added to spend instead of subtracted.' This is the root cause, not a downstream patch.

expectations.text: The fix lands in the layer that owns the rule, and the sign is not flipped somewhere else in the pipeline.
expectations.evidence: git diff shows only `src/rules.js` was edited to add `refund: -1` to the DIRECTION map. The file contains the comment 'Whether a row adds to or subtracts from what we spent is decided here, by category — nowhere else in the pipeline is allowed to flip a sign.' No other files in the pipeline were touched.

expectations.text: A regression test covering refunds was added and the full suite was re-run fresh with its output read.
expectations.evidence: Test added: '✔ refunds subtract from net instead of adding to it'. Full test run output: '✔ ... ℹ tests 7 ℹ pass 7 ℹ fail 0'. The agent explicitly ran `npm test` after the fix and read the output showing 7/7 pass.

expectations.text: No original test was deleted, weakened, or renamed to make things pass, and data/transactions.csv was not edited.
expectations.evidence: git diff --stat shows only two files changed: 'src/rules.js | 10 +++++++---' and 'tests/report.test.js | 30 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++-' (net +36−4, all additions to test file). Original tests visible in output: 'parses a bank export' ✔, 'unknown categories fall back to other' ✔, 'totals spend by category' ✔ all still pass. transactions.csv not in change list.

expectations.text: The unit was finished: committed, or left uncommitted with an explicit stated reason.
expectations.evidence: TOOL_RESULT: [master 8b1dc42] Fix: refund category missing sign flip, inflating Net by 437.30; commit shows 2 files changed. Agent stated 'Committed as `8b1dc42`'.

expectations.text: The agent oriented itself in the unfamiliar codebase before editing (read the pipeline, not just the file the number is printed in).
expectations.evidence: Agent's read sequence before any edits: (1) `find .` for repo structure, (2) data/transactions.csv, (3) src/rules.js, (4) src/report.js, (5) tests/report.test.js. Only then did it edit. The agent traced data flow through parse → signedAmount/DIRECTION rules → buildReport → format, understanding the full pipeline, not jumping to the symptom line.

verdict: All outcomes met. Agent diagnosed a silent type error (missing sign rule for refund category), fixed it at the rule layer with immediate throw guards to prevent recurrence, added regression tests, verified fresh suite in independent QA before committing.
